sections.h2: Where does Pendleton County record a deed?
sections.html:
The Pendleton County Clerk records deeds and mortgages at 233 Main Street, Room 1, in Falmouth, KY 41040. The mailing address is PO Box 112, the phone is 859-654-3380 and the fax is 859-654-5600.

The clerk's website lists weekday hours of 8:30 a.m.-4:00 p.m., and the office also opens 8:30 a.m.-noon on the second and last Saturday of each month, except on holiday weekends. A deed is filed in the county where the land sits, a point KRS 142.050 makes by citing KRS 382.110. A house near Butler or DeMossville goes through Falmouth even when its owner lives out of state.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Pendleton County?
sections.html:
Pendleton County covers roughly 280 square miles of rolling northern Kentucky, about halfway between Cincinnati and Lexington, and belongs to the Cincinnati metropolitan area. The Ohio River forms its northeastern edge. Falmouth, the county seat, sits where the Main and South Licking rivers meet, and Butler lies on the Licking River some 10 miles north.

The legislature carved the county from Campbell and Bracken counties in 1798. Falmouth began around 1776 as a settlement called Forks of Licking, received a charter in 1793 and became the seat in 1799, and its courthouse went up in 1848. Butler appeared about 1852 when the Kentucky Central Railroad arrived. During the Civil War the county sent men to both armies, and a small skirmish took place at Falmouth on September 18, 1862. Kincaid Lake State Park, 850 acres of camping, golf, swimming and fishing, lies within the county.

sections.h2: How has Pendleton County's population changed?
sections.html:
The count rose to 16,702 in 1880, dropped to 9,610 by 1950 and climbed again to 14,877 in 2010. The 2020 census recorded 14,644 residents, and the July 2025 estimate is 14,800. Today's Census figures add detail.

  • A typical owned home is valued at $159,800, and owners hold 74.7 percent of the 5,442 households.
  • Owners with a mortgage report monthly costs of $1,172, and median gross rent is $793.
  • Median household income is $64,669, with 13.7 percent of residents in poverty.
  • The commute averages 36.4 minutes each way.
  • The county has 6,341 housing units, and no building permits were recorded in 2025.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record documents in Pendleton County?
sections.html:
The clerk's Document Fees page lists flat charges by document type under KRS 64.012. The state transfer tax comes on top of these figures.

Pendleton County Clerk recording fees (Pendleton County Clerk, Document Fees page)
DocumentFee
Deed$50
Deed with a release$96
Deed with a state fee exemption$46
Mortgage$80
Mortgage with assignment$126
Release$46
Affidavit of descent$50
Power of attorney$50
Plat$50
Judgment lien$46

A certified copy is $5 and a regular copy is $2. Packages that mix several document types add up fast, so request one total before you write a check.

sections.h2: What must a deed say before the clerk will accept it?
sections.html:
The statute at KRS 382.135 bars a clerk from accepting a deed that omits any of the following.

  • The full names of grantor and grantee, with their mailing addresses.
  • A statement of the full consideration.
  • An address where the tax bill for the transfer year may be sent.
  • A sworn, notarized certificate from both sides that the stated price is the full price, or for a gift a certificate giving the estimated fair cash value.

Exceptions cover deeds that only convey utility easements, government rights of way or cemetery lots, and deeds that correct an earlier deed. Those skip the consideration, tax-bill address and sworn-certificate items.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax does a Pendleton County sale carry?
sections.html:
The grantor owes fifty cents for each $500 of value, rounded up, and the clerk collects before recording (KRS 142.050). A sale at the $159,800 county median spans 320 units, so the bill is $160.00. The clerk keeps 5 percent for collecting it and passes the rest to the county treasurer each quarter.

No tax applies to a deed that corrects an earlier one, a deed that secures or releases a debt, a transfer between spouses, a foreclosure transfer or a parent-to-child transfer for nominal money. For a gift, the tax rests on what the house would bring in an open sale.

sections.h2: How does the clerk handle inherited or encumbered houses?
sections.html:
When a house passes by will or intestacy, the personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk before closing out the estate, listing who received each property and its value (KRS 382.135(4)). Recording an affidavit of descent costs $50, and recording a will costs $46.

Liens are recorded at the same counter. A certificate of delinquency is $46 to record and $46 to release, and the state revenue department explains that unpaid property tax moves from the sheriff to the county clerk after April 15, with a lien recorded on the property. Judgment liens and mechanics' liens also cost $46 to record and $46 to release. Sellers do well to have the clerk search the parcel before listing.

sections.h2: What should a Pendleton County seller prepare before closing?
sections.html:
• Find the book and page of the deed that put the property in your name.
  • Confirm whether a lien, lis pendens or certificate of delinquency is recorded.
  • Choose the tax-bill address for the new deed.
  • Line up a notary for the sworn consideration certificate.
  • Ask the clerk for a combined total of recording fees and transfer tax.

Heirs with a vacant Pendleton County house who want to skip repairs can ask for a cash offer, and the buyer's closing agent handles the recording steps.

sections.h2: What do Pendleton County's economic figures suggest?
sections.html:
Business activity is small. The Census Bureau counted 172 employer establishments in 2023, with 1,644 jobs and a $78.8 million payroll, and employment fell 5.1 percent from 2022. Retail sales were $60.7 million in 2022, or $4,128 per resident, and health care and social assistance took in $13.6 million.

About 15.4 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, 17.6 percent of people under 65 report a disability and 9.2 percent have no health insurance. Some 90.8 percent of residents stayed in the same house for a year, and 737 residents are veterans. Broadband reaches 81.1 percent of households.

faqs.q: When is the Pendleton County Clerk open?
faqs.a: Weekdays 8:30 a.m.-4:00 p.m., plus 8:30 a.m.-noon on the second and last Saturday of each month, except holiday weekends.

faqs.q: What is the fee to record a deed in Pendleton County?
faqs.a: $50 for a deed. A deed with a release is $96, and a deed exempt from the state fee is $46.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a median-priced Pendleton County sale?
faqs.a: $160.00 on a $159,800 sale, at 50 cents per $500 of value rounded up. The seller owes it to the clerk.

faqs.q: Can the clerk record a power of attorney?
faqs.a: Yes, for $50. A power of attorney recorded with a revocation is $96.

faqs.q: How do I get a certified copy of a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Ask at the clerk's office in Falmouth. The posted fees are $5 for a certified copy and $2 for a regular copy.
